fields.statement: Verified bebbb7d91 under the capped scope with RHIZA_/SHIP_/REX_ unset. Exit 0: go test ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/run-intervention-approve$; the 9 named neighbour scripts (autonomy-accept-rule, owner-run-gate-accept, inbox-owner-run-accept, run-worktree-carries-accept, run-status-interventions, run-signoff-workflow-owner, review-signoff, review-signoff-autonomous, lifecycle); go test ./internal/api -run 'Accept|Reject|Lifecycle|Gate|Intervention|Signoff|Approve'; go vet ./internal/api; rhiza ship generate (0 files staged); rhiza render. The Checks line for the 64 accept/reject scripts was a placeholder, so I rebuilt the list as the scripts containing 'rhiza accept|reject' and 'run start' (exactly 64). They passed twice; one earlier run printed FAIL with no output kept, under load average 8.7 on 4 cores, and did not happen again. The script covers each acceptance point: an owner accept under auto accept makes intervention_count 1 with kind approve, step hold and actor test; an owner reject of a live run journals approve too; a dry run journals none; a run whose workflow declares accept owner journals none; an accept with no live run leaves every run's count unchanged; rhiza run approve at a waiting signoff gives succeeded with intervention_count 0. From the diff: journalApprove runs only when rule == owner and not on a dry run. The workflow's own gate (run_review.go:1843) always accepts under rule autonomous or autonomy, so it never journals. rhiza run approve (run_signoff.go) is untouched and never calls journalApprove. A journal error only prints a warning, so accept, reject and approve behave as before. Nothing changed outside the leaf's files (the test workflow's own autonomy setting covers run_signoff.go). No TODOs or stubs.
